text:
Maya: opened a small PR that adds Windows agent notes, ARM64 packaging tips, and a short nftables vs iptables troubleshooting section for Private installs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1533 :memo:

Ethan: Nice. Can you call out the exact kernel versions we support for nftables? Some customers hit weird conntrack behavior on older kernels.

Maya: Added a table in the networking appendix: recommended kernels >=5.10 for nftables, fallback steps for iptables-legacy on 4.x series. Also a note on conntrack table sizes and the recommend sysctl values.

Sharon: For the Windows agent section 5a5, can we include a sample NSSM service file and a note about firewall inbound rules? A few customers deploy on Windows Server and they miss the outbound proxy bits.

Maya: included both. Example NSSM commands and a PowerShell snippet: 
```powershell
# install as service via nssm
& nssm install redwood-agent C:\ProgramFiles\Redwood\agent.exe \--config C:\etc\redwood\agent.yaml
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Redwood Agent Outbound" -Direction Outbound -Action Allow -RemotePort 443
```

Carlos: HSM section: please add SELinux file context guidance for common PKCS#11 libs on RHEL/CentOS. I've seen lib loading fail due to wrong context. Suggest: chcon -t textrel_shlib_t on the .so.

Maya: added SELinux note and an example restorecon workflow too. Also added vendor path examples for SoftHSM (/usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so), YubiHSM2 (/usr/lib64/libyubihsm.so), and a catch-all env var REDWOOD_PKCS11_PATH.

Ethan: One more: the installer flag you introduced is called --force-min-routes. Can you make the docs explicit that it only relaxes the BGP route checks and does not change pod networking mode? Customers confused it was switching CNI modes.

Maya: done, clarified language and linked to the installer reference table. I also added INSTALLER_EGRESS_IFACE to the flags table with examples for AWS, GCP, and on-prem NIC names.

Sharon: Did you add a Windows networking preflight? We need to recommend checking WinHTTP proxy settings and that the service account can read the cert dir.

Maya: yep, small preflight check for netsh winhttp show proxy and PowerShell to test TLS: 
```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://staging.docs.redwood-inference.internal/ -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 5
```

Carlos: Link-checker flagged one anchor mismatch in packaging.md (#arm-package vs #arm64-package). Also saw a lint warning about 'registries' pluralization in a sidebar link.

DocOps Bot: docs-ci/build #629 started (sha: a1b2c3d) staging: https://staging.docs.redwood-inference.internal/priv-win-arm-1533

Ethan: For ARM packaging, can you include the checksum step for the tarball and an example of using gpg --verify for signed releases? Some of our offline customers demand signature verification.

Maya: added both: sha256sum example and gpg --verify with a note to keep public keys in /etc/pki/rpm-gpg or /usr/local/share/keys. Also added a short note about cross-compile caveats for musl vs glibc.

Sharon: LGTM except for the anchor and the sidebar wording. I'll push a tiny fix to your branch if you want.

Maya: please do. If CI is green and no further comments from Carlos on SELinux wording, I'd like to merge before EOD. Thanks! :pray:

Carlos: I'll quickly sanity check the SELinux commands and the PKCS#11 path examples in 10m.

DocOps Bot: PR #1533 updated build queued: docs-ci/build #630

Maya: thanks all. I'll monitor staging link and reply to customers with it if they test.
